verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce is itself a programmatic REST API platform, which makes non-interactive automation plausible. It documents agent-callable endpoints (POST /acp/v1/tokens, /acp/v1/instructions, credential retrieval), a separate test host (apitest.visaacceptance.com) with a sandbox for test transactions, and an npm-published MCP toolkit. However, card enrollment and payment instructions require live cardholder passkey or OTP step-up, which limits fully unattended runs, and nothing documents CI or headless usage specifically. Missing for 10: CI/headless-specific documentation, a way to complete passkey/OTP step-up non-interactively for automated tests, and hands-on corroboration of an unattended pipeline run.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Your agents can enroll a customer's card for tokenization during the customer's account registration or when the customer begins a new purchase intent
After completing the evaluation registration process, you will be able to send test transactions
The agent requests the user to authenticate the Payment Instruction using their Passkey and provides that instruction to the Visa Intelligent Commerce platform.
The toolkit is built in TypeScript, and you can integrate it with the Vercel AI SDK or use it to access a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
